newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch insurers say they look for takeovers.
newsitem.headline: Dutch insurers say they look for takeovers.

text.p: Dutch insurers ING Groep and Aegon said on Friday they were looking for takeover and merger opportunities around the world, but Aegon said it was still not interested in a merger with a bank.

On Thursday analysts told Reuters they expected mergers involving Dutch insurers in 1997 and some said Aegon would could be interested in merging with bank ABN AMRO as soon as the United States changes its law, making it possible for banks and insurers to unite.
An Aegon spokesman said on Friday a merger with a bank was excluded for many reasons.

"Aegon-chairman Kees Storm recently said a merger between a bank and Aegon would be excluded as investors would rather decide themselves how much of their portfolio they invest in a bank and how much in an insurer," the spokesman said.
"Conglomerates (combined banks and insurers) are usually valued less than pure firms (insurers).
Storm had also said that he did not expect any U.S. mergers between banks and insurers in his lifetime.
"There's no need for such a change," Aegon said.
Several analysts said yesterday they expected the United States would alter its current law, which forbids a merger between banks and insurers, within about a year.
ING said it would not react to any rumour on takeovers or mergers.
"But we look around for good opportunities all over the world," a spokeswoman said.
Analysts expect ING to unveil a big acquisition in the United States or Europe this year.
They also expected Aegon to continue making acquisitions, although it recently announced a multi-billion purchase in the U.S.
It is buying Providian Corp's insurance activities, the biggest U.S. life insurance purchase to date and the biggest U.S. acquisition by a Dutch company.
Aegon said after it announced the U.S. takeover that it was still looking for acquisitions.
"We are able to do this because we have the money available and if there are nice opportunities, we will look at them," the company said.
